gloss: reluctant to part; sad to say goodbye

definitions.gloss: reluctant to part; sad to say goodbye; hating to leave
definitions.explanation: Describes the feeling of not wanting to separate from someone or leave a place because the time together has been so pleasant or meaningful.

examples.japanese: {別|わか}れ{惜|お}しい{気持|きも}ちでいっぱいだった。
examples.english: I was full of reluctance to say goodbye.

examples.japanese: {楽|たの}しい{時間|じかん}はあっという{間|ま}で、{別|わか}れ{惜|お}しかった。
examples.english: The fun time flew by, and I was sad to part.

examples.japanese: {留学先|りゅうがくさき}の{友人|ゆうじん}たちとの{別|わか}れが{惜|お}しくて、{空港|くうこう}で{涙|なみだ}が{出|で}た。
examples.english: I was so reluctant to part from my friends from my time studying abroad that tears came at the airport.

notes:
A compound adjective formed from {別|わか}れ (parting) + {惜|お}しい (regrettable, reluctant to lose). Expresses the bittersweet feeling of not wanting a pleasant time or relationship to end.

FORMS:
- {別|わか}れ{惜|お}しい: predicate (parting is sad)
- {別|わか}れ{惜|お}しそうに: in a way that shows reluctance to part
- {別|わか}れが{惜|お}しい: separated form with the same meaning

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {別|わか}れ{惜|お}しい{気持|きも}ち: feelings of reluctance to part
- {別|わか}れ{惜|お}しそうに{手|て}を{振|ふ}る: to wave reluctantly in farewell
- {名残|なごり}{惜|お}しい: a near-synonym meaning reluctant to part (more literary)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {名残|なごり}{惜|お}しい: reluctant to part — very similar but slightly more literary; can also apply to leaving a place or ending an experience
- {寂|さび}しい: lonely, sad — broader emotion of loneliness, not specifically tied to parting
- {切|せつ}ない: painfully tender — a deeper, more wrenching emotional pain
